investigations.question: Do the supplied benchmark snapshots expose the expected country-code keys and year fields needed for the Western Asia join and the requested internal renewable water resources per capita formula?

Can the full Western Asia workflow preserve all 18 benchmark country rows, join the three 2021 country tables by exact code, derive the internal-only per-capita value, and classify it into quantiles with a separate No data category?

investigations.findings: The supplied boundary snapshot exposes ISO_A3, SUBREGION, and benchmark_row_id, and filtering SUBREGION = Western Asia returns 18 benchmark country rows. The withdrawals and internal-share tables both expose Country Code plus a populated 2021 field. The supplied population snapshot also exposes Country Code and a populated 2021 field, so the user’s requested year is available in the supplied inputs despite the collection note mentioning a newer edition.
limitations: This trial checked source keys and year fields only. It did not yet verify successive join behavior, the derived calculation, or the final quantile classing.
investigations.next_action: Run the full Western Asia private trial to verify repeated year-field joins, the derived internal-only per-capita value, and the final No data-aware quantile classes.

investigations.findings: The Western Asia filter retained all 18 benchmark country rows. The withdrawals join matched all 18 rows by exact ISO_A3 to Country Code. The second join also matched all 18 rows, but it renamed the repeated year fields to 2021_x and 2021_y. The run then failed at share_field because it still referenced a nonexistent field named 2021 instead of the joined internal-share field 2021_y.
limitations: This run stopped before the population join, derived value, and final classing because of the corrected field-name mistake.
investigations.next_action: Run a focused correction from the retained share_join output, map internal_share_pct_2021 from 2021_y, then continue through population join, derived value, and quantile classification.

investigations.question: After correcting the internal-share field name to 2021_y on the retained two-join output, can the workflow complete the 2021 population join, derive the internal-only per-capita value, and produce the final five-quantile country classes with No data preserved?

investigations.findings: The corrected method completed successfully from the retained two-join output. The internal-share field mapped from 2021_y without changing the 18 retained Western Asia country rows. The 2021 population join matched all 18 rows. The derived field internal_water_per_capita_m3py was created, and the final classified output retained all 18 rows with a value_class field ranging from 0 to 5. One country remained unknown in the derived value and classed into the separate No data category; the other 17 countries had known numeric values.
limitations: This focused trial reused the retained two-join artifact from the earlier Western Asia join trial. The full production workflow still needs to be saved and executed as the final deliverable.
